pr_title: Create a ref-assembly package for HttpHandler
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/19202

------------------------

This adds a package to carry a ref assembly for WebAssemblyHttpHandler. The current contents resemble what's currently in the runtime, we can update it once the HttpHandler changes are in the runtime. I choose `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.HttpHandler` as the package name since it's meant to be a stop-gap until the runtime package is available in .NET 5.0. We can move this code over to dotnet/Blazor once we're ok with the shape of this change.
pr_comments:
BTW if the suggested API changes aren't possible because the refassembly has to correspond to an existing underlying implementation, totally fine to leave that until a future follow-up.

If so, and if you do agree that API changes are beneficial, would you be able to add an issue to track this?

Nothing should have a ref/ assembly unless it's in the shared framework. We removed extra ref/ projects entirely in at least 'release/3.1' though that cleanup may not be complete in 'master' or 'blazor-wasm'. Why is a ref/ assembly necessary / wanted here?

Note ref/ assemblies only add baggage to shipped packages and a slight complication to assembly resolution on user's machines. The only reason would be hiding `public` API from user's compilers. But, we shouldn't need such complications.

Bottom line, add the src/ project but not the ref/ one.
Thanks @dougbu. I realized that the project isn't a reference provider due to how it builds. Updated it and undid the changes to `ProjectReferences.props`

@pranavkm for future reference, there's a difference between being a reference provider (which means `@(Reference)` items in other projects work) and providing a ref/ **assembly** (which is about shipping something to customers in our targeting pack). And, you don't need long paths like `..\..\WebAssemblyHttpHandler\src\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.HttpHandler.csproj` in multiple places when using `@(Reference)` items.
